# Scope: the whole com.desertstormfront.graphics.table package (20 methods + 23 fields, 8 classes).
# SpriteRegion: the six ints are the six columns SpriteSheetLoader parses out of the sprite config
#   ("x y w h offX offY"), with the anchor already applied at both construction sites:
#     a = x  = col0 - col4/2        b = y = col1 - col5/2
#     c = w  = col2                 d = h = col3
#     e = offsetX = col4            f = offsetY = col5
#   The getters take the field names (see SpriteSheetLoader 120-138 and 265-304).
# TimedFrame / WeightedFrame / ProgressFrame: same shape (int + SpriteRegion) with different int
#   meaning, read from how the tables consume them:
#     TimedFrame.a    -> elapsed milliseconds for one animation step      -> duration   (a())
#     WeightedFrame.a -> pick weight of a frame inside a weighted list    -> weight     (a())
#   Their /* synthetic */ static accessors are the only readers of the fields (constructor +
#   the tables), so they inherit the same names: a(...) -> getDuration/getWeight, b(...) -> getRegion.
# SpriteAnimationSet: a = List[] indexed by facing, b = int[] total weight per facing
#   a(int, long) walks the weights with (elapsed % total) -> getRegion(direction, elapsedMs);
#   a() returns the facing count (Tables use it as the direction count) -> getListCount.
# UnitSpriteAnimation: (unitTypeId, facing) plus one base region, one progress-driven frame list
#   and one time-driven frame list, each with its own pre-computed total:
#     a -> unitTypeId, b -> facing, c -> baseRegion (returned when no progress list applies),
#     d -> progressFrames (ProgressFrame), e -> progressTotal, f -> timedFrames (TimedFrame),
#   a(boolean, float) picks the progress frame: it only animates when the flag is set, and the
#   float is the 0..1 progress (the stored duration is progress*10000) -> getProgressRegion.
#   a(long) picks by elapsed time -> getTimedRegion. a()/b() -> getUnitTypeId/getFacing.
#   Cross-check: UnitSpriteTable indexes rows by unitType.getId() and columns by
#   unit.getDirection().a(), which fixes a/b; BuildingSpriteTable does the same with
# BuildingSpriteTable / UnitSpriteTable: a = per-unit-type/per-terrain-type lists -> tables;
#   a(Site)/a(Unit) select one animation row -> getAnimationSet / getAnimation.
# No member here is reached by name (no reflection, no named persistence; a unit sprite is stored
# as a sprite-sheet index), so renaming cannot change save data or config parsing.
